collection.topic: Fourth Amendment warrantless vehicle and container searches

provenance: Original synthetic fact patterns for engineering checks; no private matters or copied headnotes.
evaluation_note: Expected matches are retrieval candidates, not exhaustive relevance judgments or validated legal answers. Preserve relevant contrary cases and identify material factual distinctions.

scenarios.title: Arrested driver and a backpack in the car
scenarios.fact_pattern: A driver is arrested for driving with a suspended license and locked in a patrol car. Officers then search a backpack on the backseat of the driver's car. Assume the driver did not consent and officers have no separately established probable cause to search for contraband.
scenarios.research_question: Find Supreme Court decisions addressing whether the arrest justifies this vehicle search, and compare decisions involving independent grounds to search a vehicle.
scenarios.initial_query: vehicle search incident to arrest secured driver suspended license
scenarios.optional_feedback: Focus on whether the driver could reach the car and whether the arrest offense would produce physical evidence in it.
comparison_checks: Distinguish a custodial arrest from issuance of a traffic citation.
Discuss access to the passenger compartment and evidence of the arrest offense separately.
Explain why probable-cause vehicle cases may still be relevant comparisons without assuming probable cause exists in these facts.

scenarios.title: Probable cause and a passenger's purse
scenarios.fact_pattern: Officers have corroborated information that drugs are being sold from a car and lawfully stop it on a public road. Assume they have probable cause to search the car for those drugs. They open a passenger's purse found in the car that could hold the drugs, although the passenger is not separately suspected of wrongdoing. No warrant or consent is present.
scenarios.research_question: Find Supreme Court decisions comparing the scope of probable cause, ownership of a container, and searches of containers inside vehicles.
scenarios.initial_query: automobile probable cause passenger belongings container search
scenarios.optional_feedback: Keep cases where suspicion concerns one specific container separate from cases where probable cause concerns the car generally.
comparison_checks: Distinguish searching belongings found in a vehicle from searching a passenger's body.
Connect the object sought with the places capable of concealing it.
Explain the difference between probable cause concerning a vehicle generally and probable cause limited to a particular bag.

scenarios.title: Covered motorcycle beside a home
scenarios.fact_pattern: An officer has probable cause to believe a motorcycle is stolen. It is covered by a tarp at the partly enclosed top of a driveway adjoining the suspect's home. Without a warrant, the officer enters that area and lifts the tarp to inspect identifying information. Assume the suspect lives at the home and there is no consent, hot pursuit, or emergency.
scenarios.research_question: Find Supreme Court decisions addressing whether automobile-search authority supplies a right to enter the area beside the home, and distinguish searches of vehicles on public roads.
scenarios.initial_query: automobile exception motorcycle driveway curtilage warrantless entry
scenarios.optional_feedback: Prioritize the vehicle's location and the officer's lawful access, not vehicle mobility alone.
comparison_checks: Identify which facts may matter to whether the driveway area is curtilage instead of assuming every driveway is identical.
Separate probable cause to search a vehicle from lawful access to the place containing it.
Preserve the limitation that Collins left other possible grounds for the search to be considered on remand.
